The board integrates a CH340C USB-to-UART programming circuit and an AMS1117-3.3V regulator, allowing the board to be powered directly from a 5V supply while providing regulated 3.3V power for the ESP32, TFT display and microSD card.

Unlike compact ESP32 boards with limited accessible I/O, this board brings the available ESP32 GPIOs to edge-mounted headers, following the familiar arrangement of a 38-pin ESP32 development board. This allows the integrated display and SD card to be used while still providing GPIO access for additional sensors, modules, peripherals and custom hardware.

The TFT and microSD card share the same SPI bus, with separate chip-select signals, allowing both peripherals to operate efficiently using the ESP32’s hardware SPI interface. ESP32 documentation identifies GPIO18, GPIO19 and GPIO23 as the conventional VSPI clock, MISO and MOSI signals respectively.

What Is the Arduino Sensor Kit 37 in 1?

The Arduino sensor kit 37 in 1 brings together the sensor and control modules most commonly used in microcontroller projects, packed in a single organised case. Instead of buying a relay module here, a flame sensor there and a joystick somewhere else, you get one box that covers temperature, light, sound, motion, magnetism and user input.

Every module in this 37 in 1 sensor kit comes on its own small breakout board with clearly marked pins, so you can wire it to your board with jumper wires and start testing straight away — no soldering required.
It is built for 5V microcontroller boards, which makes it a natural match for the Arduino UNO, Nano and Mega families.

Big Reed Module / Double Color LED Module
Which Boards Does the 37 in 1 Sensor Kit Work With?
The modules in this sensors kit for Arduino are designed around 5V logic, which covers the most widely used Arduino boards:
Arduino UNO — the standard choice for learning and for most tutorials written around this kit
Arduino Nano — same microcontroller in a smaller footprint
Arduino Mega 2560 — when a project needs more I/O pins than the UNO offers

Several modules in the kit output an analog signal rather than a simple on/off reading — the photosensitive resistor, the analog hall sensor and the microphone module among them. Boards without an analog-to-digital converter cannot read these directly and need an external ADC. That is worth checking before you plan a build around a board other than the Arduino families above.
You will need jumper wires to connect the modules to your board. A breadboard is useful but not required for most of them.

blocks.text: Where to use the UA741 Op-amp

If you have been into electronics for quite some time and have started with Op-Amps then you should have for sure come across the name UA741. It is a single-package Op-Amp that has been widely used by engineers and students for quite a long time now. This Op-Amp can be used for many general-purpose applications like Voltage followers, Buffers, Comparators, Amplifiers, Adders, and much more. So if you looking for a plain old Op-Amp just for some basic circuit design then this IC might be the right choice for you.
Although there are dozens of other Op-Amps with advanced technology, the UA741 still seems to be the first choice for many engineers because of its reliable properties

UA741 IC is very similar to the LM324 Op-Amp, and the LM324 can be considered as a successor for the UA741. The main difference is that LM324 has two Op-Amps inside package making to more cost effective and compact. If you are curious to learn about few application circuits of this IC then you can read through how LM324 is used since both the IC shares the same applications.

Other than that one notable unique feature of the UA741 Op-Amp is that it has two Offset pins (pin1 and pin 5). These two pins can be used to correct the offset error of an Op-Amp. That is when the voltage difference between the inverting and no-inverting pins are zero the output voltage of the Op-Amp should also be zero. If not then it is considered as offset error and it can be brought to zero again by providing a offset voltage through the offset pins that would nullify the error.

The Op-Amps as we know are the work horse for most electronics circuit designs. There are a plethora of application circuits for Op-Amp each having its characteristics and significance in its own way. But every Op-Amp designs will have some common design considerations or tips which are common among them and we will discuss the same further.

Inputs: Op-Amps are known for its high input impedance, meaning it will not draw any current (or disturb) the signal that is being given to the Input pin. The input stage of an Op-Amp is mostly complex since it involves many stages. The Input common-mode range value must be considered while supplying voltage signals because the input voltage should never exceed the rail voltage else it will create a latch-up condition which in return will create a short circuit of the supply voltage and thus damaging the circuit permanently. Also the difference between the voltage values of the Inverting and the Non-Inverting pin should not be more than the Differential Input Voltage Rating.

Output: The UA741 is not a rail to rail Op-Amp hence the output voltage will not reach the maximum positive or maximum negative voltage when saturated. It will always be ~2V less than the supply voltage, this voltage drop occurs because of the Vce voltage drop of the transistors present inside the Op-Amp. Also remember that a saturated Op-Amp will comparatively draw more current and thus results in power loss.

Gain/Feedback: Op-Amps are known for their very large Open-Loop Gain, but sadly this gain is accompanied by noise hence most of the circuits are designed using Closed-Loop. A Closed-Loop system provides feedback to the input this limiting the gain value of the Op-Amp and the noise associated with it. A Negative feedback is commonly preferred, since it has predictable behaviour and stable operation.

The XD-82B is a battery level indicator module for 12V batteries. It measures the battery voltage and shows the remaining charge on a 4-segment LED bar, so you can see the battery status at a glance without a multimeter. It is small, simple to wire with just two connections, and easy to mount in a panel or project box.
Connection: 2 wires: battery positive and negative

Check the polarity before connecting. Add a small switch in the positive wire if you only want to check the level from time to time, because the indicator draws a small current whenever it is connected.
12V battery boxes and portable power stations

The more segments that light up, the higher the battery voltage. Since the module reads voltage, the bar drops temporarily under a heavy load and recovers when the load is removed. For the most accurate reading, check the battery at rest.
The level steps are set for 12V batteries; on other voltages or chemistries the display will not match the real charge.
Keep the wires short and well insulated, and add an inline fuse when connecting to large batteries.

The BIGTREETECH Kraken V1.0 motherboard is a 32-bit printer motherboard developed by the 3D printing team of Shenzhen Biqu Technology Co., Ltd. for large machines. It is driven by a high-voltage and high current stepper motor, greatly simplifying the connection between the motherboard and the high-voltage drive, and greatly saving installation space in the chassis. The motherboard adopts ID designed silk screen printing, paired with ID designed heat sink for auxiliary heat dissipation, which is both beautiful and practical.
*Using a 32-bit ARMCortex-M7 series STM32H723ZGT6 main control chip with a main frequency of 550MHz;

*The power chip adopts TPS5450-5A and supports DC12/24V power input. The output current of the chip can reach up to 5A, and the peak value can be Up to 6A, perfectly supporting Raspberry Pi power supply;
*The motherboard reserves a BOOT button, and users can update the motherboard boot program through DFU;
*Increase the protection circuit of the thermistor section to prevent the main control chip from burning out due to leakage of the heating bed or heating rod;
*The CNC fan has optional voltages of 24V, 12V, and 5V, eliminating the need for customers to connect external transformer modules, thereby reducing motherboard damage robability;
*On board dual MAX31865, supports dual PT thermocouples, supports two or four wire PT100/PT1000 options, convenient Customer DIY usage;
*MCU firmware can be upgraded through MicroSD cards or updated through DFU through Klipper’s makeflash command MCU firmware;
*The SPI mode of 8-way TMC2160 driver on board, with onboard DIAG function pins, can be easily accessed by simply plugging and unplugging the jump cap Can be used;
*Reserved interfaces: material breakage detection, shutdown after completion, Probe, RGB, I2C, servo interface, EXP1+EXP2, CAN UART (SBC) interface, USBA power output interface, etc;
*Using high-performance MOSFET tubes to reduce heat generation;
*Reserve two four wire fan interfaces, with optional voltages of 24V, 12V, and 5V, and can be used to connect to water cooling devices;
*Reserved proximity switch interface, supporting NPN and PNP type selection, (24V, 12V, 5V) voltage optional;
*Reserve SPI expansion interfaces for customers using Klipper firmware to connect external acceleration sensors for acceleration compensation;
*The MOSFET control power supply of TMC2160 is provided by an external DC12V, which reduces the output impedance of the driver and reduces chip heating.

The 9V Battery Snap Connector to DC Female Jack Cable adapts a standard 9V battery snap into a 5.5mm x 2.1mm female DC socket, letting you plug in any device or cable that normally expects a male barrel connector. It is the perfect companion to a DC male power cable when the connection needs to be reversed.

The PCB Prototype Board FR4 7x10cm (Dotted/Isolated Pads) is a single-sided fiberglass prototyping board where every hole has its own isolated copper pad, with no strips connecting neighboring holes. Its smaller footprint suits compact point-to-point circuits and breakout projects.
Material: FR4 fiberglass epoxy laminate for durability and heat resistance during soldering.
Copper Pattern: Individually isolated round pads at every hole, with no pre-connected tracks.
Hole Grid: Standard 2.54mm (0.1 inch) pitch, compatible with DIP components, headers, and jumper wires.
Board Size: 70mm x 100mm, a handy size for small circuits and breakouts.
Single-Sided: Copper pads on one side only, keeping the board simple to work with.
